deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics and is not in Riemann's hand. It continues an editorial preface by Karl Hattendorff, who in April 1866 received Riemann's formula-only manuscript on minimal surfaces. Hattendorff worked it up into the paper 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', submitted 6 Jan 1867 and printed in Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 13. The text continues from 55r ('Wie auf dem Gebiete der Abelschen Functionen so sind also auch') and reads: 'hier die beiden großen Mathematiker einander begegnet, und es ist interessant zu bemerken, daß die Untersuchungen beider nahezu in dieselbe Zeit fallen. Die von Weierstraß auf der einen, etc.' In English: as with Abelian functions, so also here the two great mathematicians met one another, and it is interesting that their investigations fall at nearly the same time. The page breaks off with 'etc.' The next folio gives a reworked, fuller version of the same note. That version cites Weierstrass, Monatsberichte Berlin 1866, p. 612: Weierstrass presented part of his results years earlier in the Berlin seminar. Hattendorff sets against this Riemann's statement that his manuscript dated from 1860-61, i.e. was five to six years old in April 1866. The page therefore serves only as a historical priority remark about the parallel discovery of the analytic (Weierstrass-type) representation of minimal surfaces. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Editorial priority remark: Riemann's minimal-surface investigations (manuscript of 1860-61) and Weierstrass's 1866 Berlin Monatsberichte paper 'Über die Flächen, deren mittlere Krümmung überall gleich Null ist' arose at nearly the same time, paralleling their meeting in the theory of Abelian functions.
results.modern_name: Historical note on the independent discovery of the Weierstrass(-Enneper) representation of minimal surfaces and Riemann's treatment of the Plateau problem for polygonal/straight-line boundaries
results.usually_credited_to: Weierstrass (1866) and Enneper (1864) for the representation; Riemann's work published posthumously by Hattendorff (1867)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an editorial note by Hattendorff with no mathematics. Its content, the near-simultaneity of Riemann's and Weierstrass's minimal-surface work, is already stated in the published editorial apparatus of Riemann's Werke.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'für' should read 'hier' (the sentence continues '...so sind also auch hier die beiden großen Mathematiker...').
Line 1-2: 'einen[?], der begegnet[?]' should read 'einander begegnet'. The word is hyphenated across the line break as 'einan-' / 'der'.
The page is in the editor's (Hattendorff's) hand, not Riemann's. It is a draft of the note given in fuller form on the next folio.
